neoforbric.config.title: ModRelay settings
neoforbric.config.general.hint:
§eSave your changes and restart the game to apply any setting.
§7This page controls mod translation, backups, and replacement file names.
neoforbric.config.general.hint.tip:
ModRelay (formerly NeoForbric; the Chinese name is 模组接力) reads these settings during startup. Changes cannot be applied to the current session.
§8After saving, quit the game and start it again from your launcher.
neoforbric.config.general.enable.tip:
When off, automatic mod replacement, dependency installation, and compatibility component installation stop. NeoForge still loads the files already present.
ModRelay still loads its settings screen, refreshes its own files, and records the startup result.
neoforbric.config.general.fabric.tip:
Look for a usable NeoForge port first. If a compatibility layer is still needed, install Sinytra Connector and Forgified Fabric API as required.
When off, Fabric mods are no longer handled automatically. Installed compatibility components stay in place. The compatibility layer cannot run every Fabric mod.
neoforbric.config.general.forge.tip:
Find a NeoForge build for the current Minecraft version, preferring the original mod version. Other available mod versions may also be tried.
Replace the original if a match is found. Otherwise, keep it and let NeoForge check whether it can load.
neoforbric.config.general.backup.tip:
Keep original Forge and Fabric files in mods/.neoforbric/backup/ when replacing them.
When off, originals are held temporarily and discarded after a successful replacement. Failed replacements attempt to restore them; unfinished recovery is retried on the next launch.
Duplicate cleanup always creates backups, regardless of this setting.
neoforbric.config.general.keepname.tip:
Keep the original jar name when replacing Forge or Fabric mods. The name may still contain Forge or Fabric.
When off, use the downloaded file name. If that name is occupied by a file with different contents, keep both files and report the conflict without overwriting.
neoforbric.config.restart.hint:
§7A restart may be needed after installing or enabling compatibility components such as Sinytra Connector, or after some mod replacements.
§8During an automatic restart, the game window may close briefly and reopen. If auto restart is off or fails, follow the instructions to restart manually.
neoforbric.config.restart.enable.tip:
Start a new game process automatically when a restart is required.
When off, the NeoForge error screen asks you to restart manually. Components that have not loaded take effect on the next launch.
neoforbric.config.restart.max.tip:
Limit automatic restarts within one sequence of launches to prevent restart loops.
1 allows one restart; 0 is also treated as 1. Manual launches are not limited.
neoforbric.config.restart.cooldown.tip:
Minimum time between automatic restarts within the same sequence of launches.
This only limits automatic restarts. You can still start the game manually from your launcher.
neoforbric.config.restart.keepalive.tip:
Keep the original game process running after an automatic restart. It waits for the new process and forwards its exit code so the launcher can continue receiving logs and track when the game ends.
The original process uses extra memory until the new game exits. When off, auto restart still works, but the launcher may end the session early and stop displaying live logs from the new process.
neoforbric.config.transpile.hint:
§7This page controls additional project searches, required dependency installation, and duplicate cleanup.
§8Use Port mappings to choose replacement projects. Add mods to the Skip list to exclude them from automatic changes.
neoforbric.config.transpile.crawl.tip:
If mappings and regular lookups find no usable build, search by modid, then by the display name if needed.
Turning this off only disables this additional search. Regular lookups may still match names. Files found through search must still pass the mod identity check.
neoforbric.config.transpile.strict.tip:
Name searches only accept projects whose identifier or name matches the search term or starts with it, such as bclib and bclib-neoforge.
When off, the most relevant result may be tried, which can lead to unnecessary downloads. Downloaded files still undergo identity checks. This also applies to name searches within regular lookups.
neoforbric.config.transpile.deps.tip:
Install missing required dependencies for mods installed or replaced during this launch. Optional and recommended mods are not installed.
If an installed dependency has an unsuitable version, report it without replacing it. Missing dependencies are recorded in the log and report; NeoForge makes the final loading check.
neoforbric.config.transpile.depth.tip:
How many dependency levels to follow. 1 handles direct dependencies only; 2 also handles their dependencies.
0 is treated as 1. To stop dependency installation, turn off Install required dependencies.
neoforbric.config.transpile.duplicates.t:
When Forge or Fabric jars share a modid, prefer the Forge build. Move the other files to backup only after the retained file is installed and its identity verified.
Jars containing multiple mods are considered together across the duplicate group. Mods unique to a removed jar may also be lost; check the report.
If a native NeoForge build already exists, corresponding foreign files stay in place. Native NeoForge duplicates are merged only when their contents are identical. This does not remove all older versions automatically.
neoforbric.config.network.hint:
§7If a download fails, keep the original file and record the reason. Whether the game can continue depends on NeoForge compatibility and dependency checks.
§7Temporary failures are retried on the next launch. Confirmed missing results are cached until they expire or relevant settings change.
neoforbric.config.network.deadline.tip:
Total time allowed to download one file, including retries and changes of download address. 0 means no limit.
Project and version lookups before the download are not included. On timeout, stop this download and keep the original file.
neoforbric.config.network.stall.tip:
Disconnect and try to resume after this long without receiving data. 0 disables stall detection.
A short timeout may interrupt slow connections unnecessarily. Resuming depends on server support and the state of the partial file.
neoforbric.config.network.retries.tip:
Maximum attempts for each candidate address, including the first request. 3 means one initial attempt and up to two retries. 0 is treated as 1.
Continue from partial data when possible; otherwise, restart the download.
neoforbric.config.network.threads.tip:
Files being queried, downloaded, and verified at once. Default: 2; range: 1–128.
Ranges within each file are configured separately. Both share the request limits.
neoforbric.config.network.mirror.tip:
Enable alternate addresses for supported official endpoints, such as an alternate official CDN. They all stay on official domains and no third-party service is contacted.
When off, official alternates are no longer expanded. Separately enabled third-party mirrors and custom addresses are unchanged.
neoforbric.config.network.thirdparty.mod:
Allow access to a third-party Modrinth address. Off by default. The built-in default is the community MCIM mirror (mod.mcimirror.top/modrinth/v2).
This project's registration and access scope with that service are still being confirmed, and its terms are not confirmed here. Both switches must be on before it is contacted, and the log names that host. While this is off, no third-party address is contacted even when Use a third-party Modrinth source is on. An address that points at a removed service (CurseForge) is refused with an explanation.
neoforbric.config.network.thirdparty.git:
Allow access to github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com through a third-party proxy (default gh-proxy.com). Off by default.
Only used when a download address points at GitHub. Check that proxy's own terms before enabling it.
neoforbric.config.network.mr.official.ti:
Query Modrinth through api.modrinth.com. On by default, and the default download source.
This controls regular mod lookups. Turning it off does not prevent every dependency lookup from using the official address.
neoforbric.config.network.mr.mirror.tip:
Query Modrinth through the address in source.modrinth.mirror.api. Allow third-party Modrinth mirror must also be on. Off by default; that key defaults to the built-in community MCIM mirror, and an empty value falls back to it.
When off, only the official API is used. A mirror switch left in an older config file does not take effect on its own.
neoforbric.config.ports.hint:
§7Choose NeoForge port projects to try first for Forge or Fabric mods.
§7One entry per row: §fsource modid = project[,project…]§7. Multiple projects are tried in the order entered.
§7Removing an entry restores automatic handling. To leave a mod unchanged, use the §fSkip list§7. Deleting the mapping file restores the built-in defaults.
neoforbric.config.ports.hint.tip.1: Full format: source modid = target[,target…][@expected modid]
neoforbric.config.ports.hint.tip.2: §8Use a Modrinth project ID or slug. mr: / modrinth: pick the source explicitly, any: searches the enabled sources.§c A bare number is a CurseForge project ID; CurseForge access was removed in this version, so such a target is skipped with a message and is never read as a Modrinth ID.
neoforbric.config.ports.hint.tip.3: §8Targets are queried from left to right. The first usable build is preferred. Sources and download speeds depend on the project and connection.
neoforbric.config.ports.hint.tip.4: §8By default, the target must provide the source modid. Use @ to allow a different modid for a port. @* skips the identity check; use it only for a target you trust.
neoforbric.config.ports.list.tip: Enter one mapping per row. Invalid entries appear in red. Save and restart the game to apply changes.
neoforbric.config.ports.error: Use modid = project[,project…]. The modid and each project must be nonempty and contain no spaces.
neoforbric.config.blacklist.hint:
§7Listed mods are excluded from automatic replacement, name searches, dependency installation, and duplicate cleanup. They are also exempt from hiding.
§7Enter one modid per row, or use §fmodid = note§7. Notes do not affect handling.
§7Compatibility components may still be installed as needed. Deleting the list file restores the default empty list.
neoforbric.config.blacklist.hint.tip.1: Use this for mods you have configured manually and want to maintain yourself.
neoforbric.config.blacklist.hint.tip.2: §8If a modid appears in both Port mappings and the Skip list, the Skip list takes priority.
neoforbric.config.blacklist.hint.tip.3: §8Hide rules only affect the displayed mod list and count. The Skip list prevents automatic changes to the listed mods.
neoforbric.config.blacklist.list.tip: Enter one modid per row, with an optional note after an equals sign. Invalid entries appear in red. Save and restart the game to apply changes.
neoforbric.config.blacklist.error: Use modid or modid = note. The modid must be nonempty and contain no spaces.
neoforbric.config.debug.hint:
§7View the startup report and logs, and adjust hide rules, download caches, and timeouts.
The defaults are usually suitable. Change these settings when troubleshooting.
neoforbric.config.debug.lastrun.tip:
Show the summary from logs/neoforbric-report.json. The count is the number of handling decisions; notes and errors show only whether any are present.
§8Open the log directory below to read the detailed logs.
neoforbric.config.debug.lastrun.none: §8No startup report is available yet, or the report file was deleted.
neoforbric.config.debug.savefail:
§cThe last save failed: §f%s
§cSome changes may not have been saved. Check folder permissions, free disk space, and whether another program is using the file.
§cResolve the problem, save again, and reopen settings to verify the result.
neoforbric.config.toast.savefail.title: ModRelay settings could not be saved
neoforbric.config.toast.savefail: §7Some changes may not have been saved. Please try again. §8See Advanced for details.
neoforbric.config.debug.hide.mods.tip:
Enter one complete modid per row. Matching mods are excluded from the displayed list and count but still load.
These entries extend the built-in hide rules. Removing entries does not disable built-in rules.
neoforbric.config.debug.hide.prefixes.ti:
Enter one prefix per row. It matches an identical modid or the prefix followed by an underscore. For example, fabric matches fabric and fabric_api.
This affects the displayed list and count, not loading. These entries extend the built-in hide rules.
neoforbric.config.debug.hide.files.tip:
Enter one jar file name prefix per row to hide every mod in matching files. This affects the displayed list and count, not loading.
Names are matched by prefix, not by full file name. These entries extend the built-in hide rules.
neoforbric.config.debug.hide.names.tip:
Enter one complete mod display name per row. Matching mods are excluded from the displayed list and count but still load.
These entries extend the built-in hide rules.
neoforbric.config.debug.resume.days.tip:
How long to keep partial downloads so they can be resumed on a later launch.
Expired files are removed. The minimum is 1 day; 0 is also treated as 1 day.
neoforbric.config.debug.resume.mb.tip:
Total size limit for partial downloads in mods/ and mods/.neoforbric/downloads/.
Remove the oldest files first when the limit is exceeded. 0 means no size limit.
neoforbric.config.debug.notfound.days.ti:
How long to cache a confirmed missing build. Default: 7 days. Query again when it expires or relevant sources, mappings, or handling settings change.
Temporary network or authentication failures are not stored in this cache.
Maximum time to wait for a network connection. 0 adds no separate limit and leaves timing to the operating system. Negative values are also treated as 0.
neoforbric.config.debug.timeout.read.tip:
Time limit for one project or version lookup, including waiting for the response and reading its contents. 0 leaves successful responses unlimited.
Reading an error response still has a 3-second limit. File downloads use separate limits.
Time limit for one file download request, including waiting for the response and receiving the file. 0 leaves successful responses unlimited; reading an error response still has a 3-second limit.
File download limit on the Downloads & network page controls the total time across requests.
Wait this long after starting the new game process, then check whether it is still running. If it has exited, the restart is considered failed.
0 checks immediately; it does not disable the check. This cannot confirm that the game will finish loading.
neoforbric.config.debug.startup.tip:
Add one pause at the start of each processing round so the loading progress has time to appear. 0 adds no pause.
This is a delay before processing, not a minimum duration for the whole loading screen.
neoforbric.config.network.segmented.tip:
Download eligible large files in parallel ranges. Off by default. Ranges and a single stream now pick addresses from the same source order, so ranges are no longer pinned to one address; unsupported sources fall back to one stream within the remaining deadline.
Ranges add requests and only pay off when the server serves each range at full speed. This may help with per-connection limits, but cannot exceed total bandwidth. Size and checksum verification still apply.
Maximum ranges per file, 2–8. Default: 2.
Every range uses one request slot, so more ranges make the total and per-host request limits the bottleneck sooner.
neoforbric.config.network.segmented.thre:
Only files at least this large are split, in MB, default 16.
Smaller files always use one stream.
A range is never smaller than this, in MB, default 4.
Fewer ranges are used when the file is not large enough, and one stream is used when even two ranges do not fit.
neoforbric.config.network.maxactive.tip:
How many download requests may run at the same time across all files, default 4, valid range 2-64, range probes included.
This is not the same as Parallel downloads above: that one is how many files are processed at once, this one is how many requests are in flight.
neoforbric.config.network.maxperhost.tip:
Concurrent download requests to one host. Default: 4; effective range: 1–32.
HTTP/2 can share connections, so this limits requests rather than connections.
neoforbric.config.network.progress.files:
Show one live row for each downloading file. Ranges are combined into that file's byte progress. Remove the row when it finishes, fails, or is cancelled.
Turn this off to show only the stage's processed-file count. Downloads continue normally.
neoforbric.config.network.recommended.ti:
On this save, use one file at a time, ranges off, at most two ranges per file, a 16 MB threshold, a 4 MB minimum range, and total/per-host limits of four.
This replaces the corresponding custom values; other settings are kept. The action resets when reopened. Save and restart to apply.
neoforbric.config.debug.progress.tip:
Log stage totals, task outcomes, bytes received, and average effective throughput. Off by default.
A file summary is always written on completion or failure. Enabling this adds a progress entry about every five seconds to logs/neoforbric.log. Speed is not shown in the interface.
